fact: Ethiopia launched the AI UniPod in Addis Ababa, a national AI innovation centre by the Ethiopian AI Institute, Addis Ababa University and UNDP with the Timbuktoo Initiative; no programme or cohort is stated.
source_slug: 2026-02-19 Ethiopia launches AI UniPod to drive innovation

fact: The Ministry of Finance's budget workbook lists an Incubation Center Building Project of ETB 135,679,000 as a capital project of the Artificial Intelligence Institution.

The Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute runs the AI UniPod and the Timbuktoo Initiative, which through skills development and startup incubation are said to build an ecosystem of more than 600 young talent; no cohort of startups is named.
Hawassa Industrial Park facilities are being transformed into a technology hub, with officials saying AI and robotics are being introduced into electronics production there.
The AI UniPod hosted a 10-day Pan-African AI Ventures Residency opened on 9 November 2026 with mentorship and product development for a cohort of 51 AI startup founders from 12 African countries.
The minister visited InnoBiz-K Ethiopia, an incubation center supporting technology startups, with no programme or cohort described.
The Entrepreneurship Development Institute launched iDisruptHub on 18 May 2026, offering incubation, seed funding and acceleration tracks for startups.
GIZ states 13 incubators and one accelerator run incubation and acceleration programmes, with 1,750 startups participating in 2020-2025.
Addis Insight reports iceaddis's Venture Meda accelerator, backed by the Mastercard Foundation, selected eight startups for its third cohort with mentorship and workshops.
The document says UNDP and the Ministry of Industry launched the timbuktoo ManuTech Hub in Addis Ababa, with space to be completed in early 2025 and a first cohort then.

Innobiz-K Ethiopia, an incubation centre in the ICT Park jointly managed by the Ministry of Innovation and Technology and KOICA, was inaugurated on 22 March 2024, with no programme or cohort described.
